label: Unemployment rate (LFS, 3-month average)
description: Unemployed people as a percentage of the labour force, population aged 15 and over; three-month moving average, seasonally adjusted.
basis: persons aged 15+, LFS 3-month moving average, seasonally adjusted
comparabilityNote: CMA and Ottawa/Gatineau part values: Statistics Canada LFS, three-month moving average, seasonally adjusted (Table 14-10-0459-01). Whitehorse, Yellowknife and Iqaluit show territory-wide values (14-10-0292-01, SA series; Nunavut's published SA values equal its unadjusted values in every month since 2019, and the Northwest Territories' in about a third of months). Charlottetown shows Prince Edward Island (province-wide, same table). Brandon shows the Southwest economic region, unadjusted 3-month moving average (14-10-0462-01) because no seasonally adjusted series exists below the province: do not rank it strictly against the SA values. LFS estimates for small areas carry large sampling variability.

label: New permanent residents by intended destination, 2025
description: Number of people granted permanent resident status in the calendar year whose intended destination at landing was this CMA/CA (or Ottawa-Gatineau part). Rounded to the nearest 5 by IRCC; counts of 0-5 are suppressed. Not current residence.
basis: IRCC admissions, calendar year, CMA/CA of intended destination
comparabilityNote: Ottawa and Gatineau are the Ontario and Quebec parts of the CMA. IRCC publishes Nunavut only as 'Other - Nunavut', so Iqaluit has no value.

label: Change in new permanent residents vs previous year
description: Percent change in calendar-year permanent resident admissions (intended destination) from the previous calendar year; computed from IRCC values rounded to the nearest 5.
basis: (admissions this year / previous year - 1) x 100
comparabilityNote: Imprecise for small places because of rounding and suppression.

label: New permanent residents per 1,000 residents
description: Calendar-year permanent resident admissions by intended destination per 1,000 residents (StatCan July 1 population estimate for the same year and geography; persons per 1,000 residents).
basis: IRCC admissions / StatCan 17-10-0148-01 July 1 population x 1000
comparabilityNote: Numerator is intended destination at landing, denominator is all residents; not a measure of immigrant share.

label: Immigrant retention in intended province, 5 years after admission
description: Of immigrant taxfilers admitted in 2018 whose intended destination was this province, the share still filing tax there in 2023: stayed / (stayed + out-migrated). Province value shown for each place in the province (flagged provincial_value).
basis: IMDB tax-record residence (postal code), taxfilers aged 15+, all admission categories, both sexes, 2018 cohort
comparabilityNote: Province-level; does not count people who moved in from elsewhere. No values for territories.

label: Immigrant retention in intended CMA, 5 years after admission
description: Of immigrant taxfilers admitted in 2018 whose intended destination was this CMA, the share still filing tax in the same CMA in 2023: stayed / (stayed + out-migrated).
basis: IMDB tax-record residence, taxfilers aged 15+, all admission categories, 2018 cohort
comparabilityNote: CMAs only; no census agglomerations or territories. Fredericton has no value because the CMA is new in the 2021 geography.

label: Median wages of immigrants five years after admission (2018 cohort)
description: Median wages, salaries and commissions of immigrant taxfilers aged 15+ admitted in 2018, in the 2023 tax year (5 years after admission), all admission categories, both sexes. Values of 0 and 1 dollars excluded from medians.
basis: 2023 constant dollars; geography is residence (postal code) when filing; provincial value (provincial_value) where no CMA value exists
comparabilityNote: Composition of the cohort differs by place (admission category, age, occupations). Not a forecast for a new arrival. No territories in the table.

MBM regions differ from CMAs (named cities, or population classes such as 'Ontario, population 100,000 to 499,999'); several places share one regional value. Annual dollars for a reference family of four, not per person.
label: MBM basket - food (reference family, per year)
description: Food: the cost of a nutritious diet (per the National Nutritious Food Basket) prepared at home. Annual cost for the MBM reference family (2 adults + 2 children; Nunavut: 2 adults + 3 children), 2025 current dollars, 2023-base MBM. To approximate other household sizes, StatCan's MBM uses a square-root equivalence scale: the cost for a household of n persons is the reference-family (4 persons) cost x sqrt(n/4); e.g. 1 person = 50%, 2 persons = 71%, 3 persons = 87%, 5 persons = 112%. Published family-size totals in table 11-10-0104-01 follow this scale.
basis: Market Basket Measure (2023 base), reference family of four, current dollars, annual
